title: L4 Reading
instructions: 閱讀下列文章，回答問題。
passage: For centuries, people believed that the Great Wall of China could be seen from the Moon. The idea appeared in books, classrooms, and even quiz shows. It sounded amazing—but it is not true.

Astronauts who have traveled to the Moon report that no human-made structures are visible from that distance. Even from a much lower orbit, the Great Wall is very hard to see because it is narrow and its color is similar to the land around it. Highways and airports, which are wider and brighter, are actually easier to spot.
Why did the myth last so long? Part of the reason is that it was repeated so often that people stopped questioning it. The story reminds us that even popular "facts" deserve a second look.

questions.q: What popular belief does the passage discuss?
options: The Great Wall is the longest wall in the world.
The Great Wall can be seen from the Moon.
The Moon can be seen from the Great Wall.
questions.explain: 第一段即點出這個說法。

questions.q: Why is the Great Wall hard to see from space?
options: It is covered by clouds all year.
It is narrow and blends in with the land.
questions.explain: 第二段：narrow and its color is similar to the land around it.

questions.q: The word "spot" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ____.
questions.explain: spot 在此為動詞「看見、發現」= notice。

questions.q: What lesson does the writer want readers to learn?
options: Highways are more important than walls.
We should question commonly accepted ideas.
questions.explain: 最後一句：even popular "facts" deserve a second look.
